questions.q: What is the core difference between dbt Cloud and dbt Core?
options: dbt Cloud is a hosted platform with a browser IDE and scheduler; dbt Core is the free, open-source CLI you install and run yourself
dbt Core is a paid product and dbt Cloud is always free
dbt Cloud only works with Snowflake, dbt Core only works with BigQuery
They use completely different SQL syntax for models
questions.explain: dbt Cloud is the hosted platform (including the Studio IDE); dbt Core is the free, open-source command-line tool you install and run yourself.

questions.q: What does the `dbt debug` command check, according to this lesson's real terminal screenshot?
options: dbt/Python versions, profiles.yml and dbt_project.yml validity, git, and the warehouse connection
The number of rows in every table in the warehouse
Whether the user has an active dbt Cloud subscription
The contents of every model's compiled SQL
questions.explain: dbt debug validates the profile and project files, checks for required dependencies like git, and finally tests the actual warehouse connection.

questions.q: Which of these is true about ref() calls, tests, and the dependency graph?
options: They work identically whether you're using dbt Cloud or dbt Core
They only work in dbt Cloud
They only work in dbt Core
They require a separate license depending on which tool you use
questions.explain: Neither tool changes what a ref() call, a test, or the dependency graph means — those are identical in both dbt Cloud and dbt Core.

questions.q: How do you install dbt Core, per this lesson?
options: pip install dbt-core plus the adapter for your warehouse, e.g. dbt-snowflake
Download a desktop app from the App Store
It comes pre-installed with Snowflake
You must request a license key from dbt Labs first
questions.explain: dbt Core is installed via pip, along with the adapter package for your specific warehouse (e.g. dbt-snowflake for Snowflake).

questions.q: What does this lesson mean by saying neither dbt Cloud nor dbt Core is 'more real' dbt?
options: A .sql file with a ref() call means the same thing in either tool — the underlying project and logic don't change
dbt Cloud and dbt Core produce different query results for the same model
Only one of the two actually connects to a real warehouse
dbt Core is being deprecated in favor of dbt Cloud
questions.explain: The tooling differs, but the actual dbt project — the models, ref() calls, tests, and dependency graph — is identical either way.
